answers.text: Gravity No matter how high I float or how light I feel, it's always there, pulling me back down, reminding me that every rise ends.
Buoyancy no matter how deep I dive or how heavy I try to feel, it's always there pushing me back up, reminding me that every plunge ends
No matter how heavy I try to feel The world keeps lifting me, nudging me toward the open air and away from the roots I want to touch
My biggest problem... I can't stay
I can't move The more the wind piles sand, the deeper I sink
staying in step My biggest problem is slip by a fraction and the whole tower runs either early or late
burn oBh The longer the more I soak it up until my skin starts to flake and glow.
It's cold. The longer I pour it, the deeper it seeps in until my skin turns brittle and pale I'm built to chill this entire ring
aheC Light Too much of it floods the mirror, scatters and scaulds the sensors I'm here to protect
Staying cool Sunlight from 100 mirrors pours into me all day packing the salt inside with more heat than steel ought to hold
My biggest problem is... Darkness I wait in an ocean of it, straining for the few stray photons that pass my way The abyss keeps most of them for itself
Pressure Down here, every movement pushes against me water, weight the sounds of the whole ocean leaning in
Dust It drifts in on the wind, settles in my grooves and starts to bridge the voltage I'm supposed to hold apart
barnacles grit and kelp Try to hitch a ride on my skin every hour. The more they build, the more drag I carry and the slower the rotor turns
ICE It creeps between the cable strands and under my pad, turning my grip into a skating rink. Every clamp grinds meltwater and shavings that can glaze my lining or corrode the housing
Every burst of spray crossed my prisms, bending the beam until it frays and fades. If I don't clear it, ships lose their line through the dark.
My biggest problem is dust. Every gust carries it dry as powder quick to fog my face and scatter the signal A thin coat is enough to mute the whole array
